title: Delayed activation
subtitle: Place the warning now; make the same space dangerous later.
summary: The boss plants a harmless rune under the player, fixes its place, then activates it after a visible countdown; the player walks fully outside the circle.
overview: Kern marks one fixed disc. Its outline and eight small runes are a harmless warning. A ring contracts to the marked radius; the disc ignites on a fixed beat and stays dangerous briefly. Tavi walks fully outside before ignition. The danger ends before Kern resets. Time, not proximity or renewed aim, triggers it.
learning: Tune placement, warning duration, collision radius, ordinary walking distance, active lifetime, and recovery as separate controls.

demo.title: Test the delayed rune
phaseDescriptions: Kern plants one visible rune beneath Tavi. The outlined disc and its extent are harmless.
The position locks at 1.6 s. The ring counts down, Tavi walks out, and the fixed disc becomes dangerous from 2.9 to 4.0 s.
The glow extinguishes before Kern resets; Tavi returns for the next loop.
demo.danger: The rune's future radius is announced, but safe
demo.locked: The location is fixed; the countdown leads to ignition
demo.reducedMotion: Autoplay is disabled by the reduced-motion setting. Use the timeline slider to inspect the loop.
demo.diagramDescription: A looping diagram of delayed activation. Kern plants a circular rune at Tavi's position. A harmless outline contracts as a countdown; Tavi walks fully beyond the fixed radius before the rune ignites at 2.9 seconds. The disc stays dangerous until 4 seconds, then clears before reset.

steps.title: Does the warning define the real footprint?
steps.body: Show the complete disc, not a tiny rune at its center. Lock the location at placement and keep the warning harmless until the stated ignition beat.

steps.title: Can a walking player clear the radius in time?
steps.body: Measure from the starting point through the full disc radius plus the player's body radius. Tavi's ordinary walk reaches clear ground before activation; the countdown must cover that route.

steps.title: Is the dangerous interval unmistakable?
steps.body: Switch from outline to solid glow precisely at activation, maintain a constant hitbox while lit, and visibly extinguish it before signaling recovery.

mistakes.title: Damage begins with the warning
mistakes.body: If the outline already hurts, the promised delay is false. Keep the preview non-damaging and test the precise activation frame.

mistakes.title: The marked area follows the player
mistakes.body: Moving the disc after placement steals the announced route. Lock the coordinate, and introduce tracking as a separate, clearly signaled rule.

designNotes.title: Separate three clocks
designNotes.body: Placement ends at 1.6 s, ignition begins at 2.9 s, and danger expires at 4.0 s in this diagram. Expose these times independently instead of stretching every phase with one speed multiplier.

designNotes.title: Reserve full-body clearance
designNotes.body: An 82-unit hazard radius with a 24-unit player body needs a center distance greater than 106 units. The illustrated target is 135 units from the rune's center.

designNotes.title: Keep the center stable
designNotes.body: The eight satellite marks and shrinking ring stay centered on one planted rune. They communicate remaining time without changing the actual collision radius.

designNotes.title: Escalate by changing one promise
designNotes.body: Later phases may shorten the countdown or alter the active lifetime, but announce the new cadence before relying on it. Adding multiple sites creates a different spatial problem.

story.title: Make the rune a clock
story.body: Kern presses a stone seal into the arena. Its eight glyphs brighten while the outer ring contracts, so the delayed detonation reads as a rule of the world rather than an invisible timer.

adaptation.title: Keep the baseline response
adaptation.body: The demonstration needs only ordinary walking. A dash can add a faster answer, but it must not be the sole way to leave the announced circle before ignition.

distinction.title: Separate timing from other area rules
distinction.body: A timed rune activates after a fixed interval regardless of player proximity. A mine waits for a trigger; a marked-area strike is a brief impact; a lingering hazard emphasizes duration after an initial hit. Here the main question is whether the player can use the visible delay to leave a committed area.

lensNotes.body: The harmless outline, eight glyphs, and contracting ring reveal both the future radius and activation beat.
A fixed center and radius make the required walking route measurable with full-body clearance.
A committed disc leaves an ordinary-movement escape; standing in the warning remains safe until ignition.
Warning duration, active lifetime, and recovery create three distinct timing windows.

examples.body: A golden glow outlines the next side of the spike floor before spikes emerge. The arena-wide patch differs from Kern's small disc, but the safe warning precedes the dangerous state at a committed location.

Bomb Boulders occupy visible positions before detonating. Their multiple locations and sequential explosions make a richer pattern; the reusable ingredient is a placed object that becomes dangerous on a later beat.

Icicle Impact previews circles before ice falls on them. Unlike Kern's sustained rune, each drop is brief and can resolve in a sequence; the example isolates the readable interval between a fixed-area warning and its activation.
